family.source: task classification: an Americas championship that qualifies for a World Championship or Olympics is family Continental_Cups

stage_kind.source: task classification; the event is the FIBA Americas qualifying tournament for 2012 Olympic Games men's basketball tournament (London) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_FIBA_Americas_Championship)

hindsight_policy: World data for the FIBA pipeline. Holds format, calendar and (where listed) real entry lists and squads only. No score, result, standing, award or statistic of this event is recorded. Real qualification routes and real group draws describe the real world; a simulated career must derive the field of any edition whose qualifiers it simulates from simulated results, and must not read this file before the dates given in known_from.

known_from.note: Group composition public from the draw; second-round and medal pairings depend on results.

rule.value: The two semifinal winners qualify for the 2012 Olympics; the other three of the top five (the two semifinal losers and the 5th-placed second-round team) go to the 2012 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament.

reason.value: The United States qualified automatically for the 2012 Olympics by winning the 2010 FIBA World Championship and withdrew; Paraguay (5th at the 2010 South American Championship) was invited in its place.

usa_participation.note: In a simulated career the USA takes part only if it has not already qualified for the 2012 Olympics through a simulated 2010 World Championship; the North America sub-zone entry route (USA and Canada) applies as in 2005 and 2007.

rounds.advance: top 4 of each group to the second round; 5th placed teams are eliminated

rounds.name: Second round (single group of eight)
rounds.pairing: each team plays the four advanced teams from the other group

carryover.value: Each team carries over all points earned in the first round except those from the game against the eliminated team.
